snippet.title: Delhi’s Veg Food Is On Another Level! 🍽️💚
snippet.description:
Delhi continues to surprise with how good pure vegetarian food can be. I spent the day exploring two iconic spots that prove you don’t need meat for a mind blowing meal. From old school flavours in the busy lanes of Purani Dilli to a freshly rebuilt favourite in Pandara Road, this one turned into a proper comfort food tour.

The first stop set the tone with a layered kulhad bowl brimming with pulao, chole, palak and all the little touches that make Delhi street food special. Then I headed to a beautifully restored restaurant to try a thali loaded with classics. The freshness of the sabzis, the richness of the dal and the soft paneer all reminded me why this city’s vegetarian scene has such a loyal fanbase.

If you love simple ingredients coming together in surprising ways, this Delhi chapter is going to make you hungry. Come experience the flavours of the capital with me.

Our first stop was Tilak Kharode Wale, a name synonymous with mutton delicacies for years. From brain to tongue, trotters, and mutton keema, their menu is a treasure trove for meat lovers. We tried the trotters followed by tongue, discovering the rich flavors that make these dishes a local favourite.  

Next, we visited Patiala Shahi Food Corner, renowned for their hearty soups. Their chicken soup stood out with its thick, peppery, and buttery flavour. Its taste was elevated by a secret spice mix that adds a unique touch.  

Chawla's Chick Fish was our third destination, a haven for fried and tandoori delights. Their fried chicken and fish are crowd-pullers, with patrons enjoying their meals parked in their cars. We tried their fish tikka, made from fresh surmai fish, which was perfectly soft and meaty.  

At Kamal Meat House, another legendary joint, we indulged in chilli chicken and keema mutton. The chilli chicken was a delightful twist on the classic, featuring fried chicken tossed in butter with capsicum, onions, and three types of gravies. The keema mutton, on the other hand, was packed with robust spices and tender meat, a true treat for meat enthusiasts.  

Sachdeva Chicken Corner was next, where we sampled creamy chicken and butter chicken on Gagan’s recommendation. The creamy chicken lived up to its name, featuring a rich curry of cream, milk, and mild spices. The butter chicken, while flavorful had a pronounced tomato base that added a tangy punch.  

To conclude our walk, we visited Kalra Sweets for a sweet finale. Their gajar ka halwa and gulab jamun were freshly made, offering the perfect balance of sweetness and richness to end the evening on a high note.  

This food walk with our friend Gagan was a fascinating gustatory journey through the diverse and delicious offerings of Geeta Colony.

🚙 About the Bangalore to Ladakh Road Trip 2025

Starting Point: Bangalore, Karnataka
Ending Point: Leh–Ladakh, Jammu & Kashmir
Distance: ~3,200 km (one-way)
Vehicle: Maruti Suzuki Baleno (Yes, we are doing Ladakh in a hatchback 🚗💪)

Bangalore → Nagpur → Sagar (MP) → Agra → Jammu → Srinagar → Kargil → Leh → Nubra Valley (Diskit–Hunder–Turtuk) → Pangong Tso → Hanle → Tso Moriri → Puga → Pang → Manali → back to Bangalore.

Route Taken: Nagpur → Seoni → Lalitpur → Jhansi → Gwalior → Agra
Distance Covered: ~900 km
Driving Time: ~15–16 hours (depending on breaks and traffic)
Highways: NH44 all the way → seamless connectivity
Road Condition: Mostly excellent 4-lane roads, occasional diversions and rough patches near Seoni and Jhansi; smoother stretches closer to Agra.

🍴 Food & Stay Options (Nagpur → Agra)

Plenty of dhabas and small eateries along NH44
Good highway restaurants near Seoni, Jhansi, and Gwalior

snippet.title: 55 Saal Purani Legacy 🔥 Bilal Chicken Khureji — Buff Boti & Bheja Fry Ka Asli Dilli Taste!
snippet.description:
Bilal Chicken — Khureji, Delhi | 55 Saal Purani Legacy 🍗🔥

Dilli ke Khureji ilake ka mashhoor naam — Bilal Chicken!
Yahan ka taste sirf khana nahi, ek virasat hai jo 55 saal se chalti aa rahi hai.
Baap-dada ka diya hua hunar, aur aaj ke time ke perfect flavors — dono ka zabardast combination milta hai yahan.
Is jagah ko chalate hain do bhai — Shamshuddin aur Bilal, jinhone apne mehnat aur taste se har food lover ka dil jeet liya hai ❤️

⸻

🍽️ Specialty Dishes:

🔥 Buff ke Ghost ki Boti – Ye Bilal Chicken ki sabse khaas dish hai!
Soft, juicy aur masalon se bhari boti jo sirf yahin milti hai. Har bite mein ek dum rich aur spicy flavour.

🧠 Bheja Fry – Jo log asli Delhi taste samajhte hain, unke liye yeh dish ek treat hai.
Bilkul creamy texture ke sath masaledar fry — melt-in-mouth experience!

🥩 Seekh Kabab – Tandoor se nikalte hi aroma hi sab kuch keh deta hai.
Perfectly grilled, juicy aur smoky taste — ek baar kha liya to yaad reh jayega.

🍢 Boneless Malai Tikka – Soft, creamy aur thoda mild spice ke sath — family ke liye perfect dish.
Har bite mein malai aur masale ka balanced blend.

🍛 Chicken Changezi – Purani Delhi ka flavour, thick gravy aur tender chicken pieces ke sath.
Ek aisa taste jo roti ya naan dono ke sath kamaal lagta hai.

🧈 Butter Chicken – Creamy, buttery aur thoda sweet-spicy touch ke sath — sabka favourite.
Rich texture aur ekdum smooth gravy.

🌶️ Chicken Chatkara – Naam hi kaafi hai!
Tangy, spicy aur full of flavour — bilkul street-style Delhi wala chatkara.

⸻

****** 
India's street food is going viral. But, not for the right reasons. We see videos racking up millions of views that show Indian food as dirty, unhygienic, and absolutely unsafe to consume. Even the latest news reports speak of the same sad state of Indian street food. For instance, just last year in May, a 19-year-old died after he consumed Shawarma in Mumbai that gave him severe food poisoning. A few months back, 97 kids fell sick after consuming Pani Puri in Madhya Pradesh. This is the state of India's street food that we all love to eat. But is this really true? Is India's street food so unhygienic? To find the answers to these questions, I decided to play Hunger Games with my team members. We went to three different cities - Bengaluru, Delhi, and Kolkata to taste and test three of the most famous street foods - Shawarmas, Momos, and Puchkas. And what we found out surprised us.

TRYING! Azad Market SARDARJI MEAT WALE Ka Keema Mutton, Chicken Curry, Mutton Pulao, Mutton Soup

This was my first experience at Sardarji Meat Wale in Azad Market. The place has no board yet people are gathered. People say they serve authentic punjabi style Keema Mutton which is prepared in Dalda. Two brothers are running this place which has a live counter where the mutton is prepared. About Taarak Mehta Ka Ooltah Chashmah:
--------------------------------------------------------------------
The show is inspired from the famous humorous column 'Duniya Ne Undha Chasma' written by the eminent Gujarati writer Mr. Tarak Mehta. This story evolves around happenings in "Gokuldham Co-operative Society" and covers topical issues that are socially relevant. The show predominantly - revolves around 'Jethalaal' (Dilip Joshi) who is an uneducated Gujarati businessman. Your 'Taarak Mehta' (Sailesh Lodha), is his neighbor. 'Jethalaal' finds a friend and philosopher in 'Taarak Mehta' and often goes to him for advice whenever he is in trouble. Jethalaal's family includes his simpleton wife 'Daya Ben' (Disha Wakani) and a mischievous son 'Tapu' (Bhavya Gandhi). Tapu is a menace and a constant source of trouble to all the members of Gokuldham. They have often warned 'Jethalaal' to reform 'Tapu' or else be prepared to leave the premises. Lost hopes of being heard by his son push Jethalaal' to call his father 'Champaklal' (Amit Bhatt) from the village. This was his great idea of leashing some control over the mischievous Tapu. The opposite happens and the grandfather joins hands with the grandson to make life a roller coaster troublesome ride for Jethalaal.

snippet.title: Delhi To Manali Roadtrip | Manali Weather  Update #manali #roadtrip #travel
snippet.description:
Delhi to Manali road trip | Manali Weather Update 
"Good morning, friends! Welcome back to the channel. Today, we’re kicking off an epic road trip from the heart of India — Delhi — all the way to the beautiful mountains of Manali."

[Footage of hitting the highway]

"With around 540 kilometers to cover, the journey promises changing landscapes, bustling dhabas, winding mountain roads, and unforgettable views. Let’s hit the road!"

[Scene: Driving through Delhi outskirts – sunrise shots]

Voiceover:

"We started early in the morning to avoid the city traffic. As we left Delhi behind, the roads opened up and the first rays of the sun lit up our path. The air slowly started getting cooler as we drove ahead."

[Scene: Driving through Murthal – dhaba stop]

Voiceover:

"Our first pit stop was Murthal — a paradise for food lovers. We grabbed a delicious breakfast of stuffed parathas and hot tea at one of the famous dhabas here. Perfect fuel for the journey ahead."

[Scene: Driving on NH-44, entering Punjab and then Himachal]

Voiceover:

"The drive on NH-44 was smooth, with green fields stretching on both sides. We crossed Karnal, Kurukshetra, and then Ambala. Once we hit Chandigarh, the real fun began — the plains gave way to hills as we entered Himachal Pradesh."

[Scene: Mountain roads, tunnels, Beas River along the road]

Voiceover:

"As we climbed higher, the roads became winding and scenic. The Beas River accompanied us, flowing gracefully alongside. Each turn brought a new view — pine forests, charming villages, and cool mountain breeze."

[Scene: Reaching Kullu Valley – local culture, apple orchards]

Voiceover:

"A quick tea break in Kullu gave us a taste of local Himachali hospitality. The air here was fresh and crisp. From here, Manali was just a couple of hours away."

[Final Scene: Entering Manali – mountain peaks, market views, evening lights]

Voiceover:

"And finally, after a full day of beautiful roads, great food, and unforgettable views, we reached Manali! Surrounded by snow-capped peaks and tall deodar trees, this town feels like a postcard."

[Outro]

Voiceover:

"So that was our Delhi to Manali road trip — full of adventure, nature, and memories. If you’re planning a trip, this is one of the most scenic drives you’ll ever take. Don’t forget to like, comment, and subscribe if you enjoyed the ride. See you in the next one!"
